_comment: Every benchmark figure the blog publishes, and every prose universal that
rests on one. scripts/check_benchmark_claims.py reads this file, renders
each bound figure from the pinned artifacts in sources.json, and compares.
figures[] entry kinds:
ratio      - published as N/M or 'N of M'. numerator and denominator are JSON
pointers into the named source. A denominator that is a
known count field (n_runs, n_wrong_effect,
n_correct_effect) must be named in the same sentence or
table cell: '54/90 runs', '54 of 72 bad saves'.
number     - published as a single value. 'pointer', 'round' digits,
optional 'scale' (use 100 to turn a rate into a percent).
exempt     - not from a pinned artifact. Needs a written 'reason' and a
'reviewed' date. There is no wildcard and no blanket skip.
superseded - the post quotes what was true on its date and upstream has
since changed. Needs 'pointer', a 'reason', a 'reviewed'
date, and a 'note' string that must appear in the post and
must carry a YYYY-MM-DD date. The checker refuses a
superseded entry whose figure still matches upstream.
'context' is a literal that must appear on the same line, and 'nth' picks
one occurrence when a line repeats a token. Together they let two figures
that read the same string be verified against two different fields.
universals[] register a sentence that turns a sample into a claim about
every case. evidence.claim is all_success (success == total upstream),
equals_zero (the pointer is 0 upstream), or prose (nothing numeric backs
it, so give a reason). The checker re-evaluates the first two.
